title: Legacy Change Radar
summary: Map a code change's owners, dependencies, and review checks.
user: Maintainers reviewing agent-authored changes in large established applications who need to find changed dependency and risk surfaces before line-by-line review.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN poster asks how to harden agentic changes to a 15-year-old, 1M+ line SaaS before review.
A 226-reaction Codex request wants IDE-integrated red/green diffs and approval rather than terminal-only change review.

recurrence: One large-codebase safety request and strong demand for better change approval point to review context, not code generation, as the bottleneck.
current_workaround: Read raw diffs, run broad CI, ask the author for context, and discover touched configuration or generated artifacts late.
incumbents_and_gap: GitHub/GitLab review and IDE diff views show changed lines; CodeQL and CI run checks. They do not summarize blast radius across ownership, migrations, public APIs, and configuration as a compact review appendix.
smallest_useful_product: A CI CLI that turns a git diff into a Markdown risk card: affected owners, dependency edges, config/migration/API markers, and required named checks.
success_measure: In 30 pilot pull requests, reviewers identify a relevant non-line-level risk in at least 20% and do not increase median review time by more than five minutes.
monetization: freemium — local analysis can be open; hosted policy/ownership integrations are team value.
constraints: Run repository-local; explain every inferred edge; never claim a risk score proves correctness; support language adapters incrementally.
why_distinct: It creates a reviewable blast-radius artifact rather than another AI reviewer or diff viewer.
